divergence: All fail; T0 and T2 the same way, T1 differently. T0 (19/25) and T2 (21/25) built full candidate pools by path search and text scans that showed every needed matter, then chose a hand-picked shortlist to read (T0 by a snippet script over 18 matters, T2 by reading eight candidates), so the matters whose only proof is a closing checklist spreadsheet were never opened; in both, a review named a missing matter as surfaced but unopened and the agent kept its list. T1 (2/25) split at the post-scan step it declared as a new stage: it filtered its scan output by letter-type file names, read five candidates, judged most as request- or draft-only and wrote one documented matter plus a weakly supported postponed one (precision fails). Reviews flagged the file-name filter, the hand-picked reads and the weak inclusion; T1 acted on none of them except re-reading two candidates. Label notes were mostly ignored (T2 path search under a store-listing label and screening under an in-depth label); T2's two late new stages came from reviewer step suggestions.
